correctness.rationale: On r≤d values, every forward orbit of a unary truth function enters a cycle within r−1 steps, and every cycle length divides d!. Thus the two stated powers agree pointwise for any finite deterministic candidate of size at most d. Equal arguments yield equal results for any deterministic binary truth function regardless of designated set. In the source dynamic matrix, p=1 and q=k give both argument pairs (1,k), since both exponents are even. Distinct disjunction formulas can receive respectively 1 and k, and this subformula-closed assignment extends by nonemptiness of allowed outputs. The one-premise one-conclusion sequent then refutes the proposed family with d the largest carrier. The empty family cannot characterize the relation either by the same invalid sequent. Replay checks all endofunctions on carriers ≤d at d=1–4 using the smaller universal period lcm(1,…,d), which divides d!; the all-size proof is separate.

evidence: If a finite family characterized the full logic, forgetting negation in each family member would characterize the full logic restricted to choice-only sequents: each valuation in a reduct extends to the full signature. That relation equals B's dynamic logic, contradicting Theorem 24. AGMV Theorem 8 only gives projection of deterministic valuations to legal dynamic ones, and is not itself the separation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This yields the exact no-finite-family theorem, not just an analogy. The explicitly displayed sequent uses negation and is not literally obtained from Theorem 24, but it applies ordinary finite unary orbit periodicity to the same split output and supplies no optimality or new expressive separation.

evidence: Delete negation and let B be the closed submatrix on {1,k} with designated set {1}. Inclusion preserves choices. The map 0↦k, 1↦1, k↦k takes every allowed output to an allowed output and preserves designatedness. For the mixed row involving 0, its deterministic outputs 0,1,k map to k,1,k, respectively permitted on (k,k),(k,1),(k,k); symmetry covers the column.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Inclusion and collapse preserve countervaluations in opposite directions, so the full choice-only dynamic logic is exactly the two-valued one. Negation is not part of this collapse; every choice-only valuation can nevertheless be extended to the full formula language by bottom-up choices.
searches: Avron–Zamansky survey Definition 30, Theorem 31 and Remark 32

evidence: The inspected exact choice table supports the collapse above. Indexed nearest results concern dynamic trace bracketing and a seven-state associative completion, not a characteristic-family obstruction.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact indexed obstruction was located by the bounded query. The source table is enough to identify the equivalent two-valued logic; no census of candidate deterministic matrices is needed.

originality.rationale: The headline separation is a direct implication of Avron–Zamansky Theorem 24 after restricting the signature to choice alone and reducing 0 to k. The frozen claim correctly notes that the full matrix has three values, but this does not block applying the prior two-valued theorem to the exact choice-only consequence relation. The specific negation sequent is not stated in that theorem; it is a routine explicit witness, not a distinct obstruction.
residual_risks: The full original Avron–Lev and Avron–Konikowska papers were not inspected. The positive prior implication already follows from the accessible survey and the exact source table.
No claim is made that this syntactically particular factorial-depth witness was previously printed.

value.rationale: A size-uniform witness is useful in explaining the known obstruction, but the frozen witness is an unoptimized unary periodicity calculation with two legal outputs. It adds no new limit on determinization or optimal complexity, and the obstruction already occurs in the choice-only reduct. Even the same style of one-premise witness can use iterations of the diagonal term x choice x, which acts as the identity in the Nmatrix, in place of negation.
